hints.title: Implementing the Command interface
hints.content: Declare `class DriveCommand implements Command`. You need four methods: `initialize()`, `execute()`, `isFinished()`, and `end(boolean interrupted)`. Store the motor and power as fields set in the constructor.

hints.title: What each method should do
hints.content: `initialize()` calls `motor.setPower(power)`. `execute()` does nothing. `isFinished()` returns `true` immediately (one-shot command). `end(boolean interrupted)` calls `motor.setPower(0.0)`.

hints.title: Scheduling and running
hints.content: After defining the class, create a `CommandScheduler`, call `scheduler.schedule(new DriveCommand(motor, 0.75))`, then call `scheduler.run()` once. The scheduler will call `execute()` and then `end(false)` since `isFinished()` returns true immediately.

hints.title: Why the motor ends at 0.0
hints.content: After one call to `scheduler.run()`: it calls `execute()` (no-op), then checks `isFinished()` which returns true, then calls `end(false)` which sets power to 0.0. The test checks that the motor power is 0.0 after the command finishes.
